ai.description: *Micrixalus herrei* is a small (20–25 mm) frog with a brown back and cream-colored belly. Males exhibit a characteristic foot-flagging behavior. It is distinguished by a pointed snout and slender limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus herrei* is best distinguished by its distinct, bright white-tipped third finger, a unique trait absent in other members of the *Micrixalus* genus.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus herrei* inhabits the moist evergreen forests of the southern Western Ghats, typically found along rocky, shaded streams at altitudes between 500 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: To attract mates, male *Micrixalus herrei* perform a unique "foot-flagging" display, rhythmically extending and waving their hind legs to signal to rivals and females.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus herrei* is an egg-laying species that breeds during the monsoon. Females deposit small clutches of eggs in nests constructed within stream-bed gravel.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Micrixalus herrei* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically inhabiting streams at elevations between 500 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Kallar Dancing Frog emits a high-pitched, rhythmic series of short, metallic "tink" notes while perched on mossy rocks along fast-flowing forest streams.
